PYS-01.title: Magnetic Capsule Maze Cup
points: Pre-test every token (paperclip/washer) against the driver magnet through the actual laminated maze before the run; set aside any washer the driver cannot move. Annealed 304 stainless washers may be effectively non-magnetic, so zinc-plated steel paperclips are the reliable default token.
Glue/tape several 6mm driver magnets into a holder (bottle cap or short dowel) so the driver is too big to mouth and easier to grip; students drive with the holder, never a loose magnet.

Keep the 200 tiny 2x1mm magnets OUT of the station entirely, or sealed in an instructor-only container for a brief teacher-led demo only. Treat all magnets as controlled inventory: count in and out, use a containment tray.
Use 5-mil laminated cardstock or one thin EVA-foam sheet as the barrier, NOT the 5mm white foam-board (too thick to couple reliably).

Draw wide, generous maze paths with gentle corners; the ~390g-pull driver can snap a light token across narrow walls and cause constant wall-touch penalties. If grabby, add a second laminated sheet or thin EVA layer to soften coupling.
Brief kids that neodymium magnets pinch hard and can chip; inspect for chips and bag any damaged magnet immediately.

PYS-02.title: Oobleck Armor Arena
points: Mixing: prefer mix-in-bag (measure cornstarch and water into a gallon freezer zip bag, knead by gloved hand) so liquid is never open; keep a couple of rigid shallow bins for teams that struggle. One open mixing tray per team is over-specified.

Pre-make a teacher reference batch at about 2:1 cornstarch:water by volume. Have teams add water last, a little at a time, to a "pours slowly but resists a fast poke" target; keep extra cornstarch to stiffen runny mixes.
Strict no-sink disposal: oobleck cements drains. Whole double-bagged pad goes into the lined trash; wipe pads and gloved hands with paper towels first, then a damp wipe.

Impact protocol: use a rigid flat lid or foam-board paddle pressed with a sharp counted slap, OR repurpose the 200 g hooked weight as a fixed-height DROP onto the lidded pad. Never hang or rest the weight statically.
Score by whether the target (coin stack, EVA-foam square, or marshmallow) is crushed or marked after the fast press.

Corn allergy: hand the affected child a teacher-prepared sealed double-bagged pad so they never touch wet starch; nitrile gloves and no-eating rule for all. Tapioca/potato starch is a documented substitute if a corn-allergic child must mix (use slightly less water).

Budget about 1 lb starch per substantial pad; enforce trim-to-minimize scoring and reuse the same sealed pad between slow and fast presses. Do not require a second full fresh batch per team on redesign.

PYS-03.title: Cardboard Automata Arcade
points: Run three to four low-temperature mini glue guns at one staff station so six teams do not stall in a single queue; every gun stays staff-operated.

Make the axle hole about 1 cm OFF CENTER so the circular cam produces follower lift. Start it with a staff-controlled push pin, widen it snugly with the skewer, then have staff add a low-temperature glue bead; a centered hole in a circular cam produces no lift.
Cut cams from EVA foam (about 2.5in/6cm diameter) rather than corrugated cardboard for a cleaner profile; keep cardboard for the box frame and handle.
If the follower lifts off and rattles, weight its top with a flat washer so gravity seats it on the cam.
Add an end stop on each end of the drive skewer (washer, tape collar, or EVA bushing glued to the axle) so it does not walk out of its holes.

At the controlled staff station, start holes with a push pin, then widen with the skewer point; do not stage loose nails or screws. Tape corner-triangle gussets to keep the box square so the axle does not bind.

PYS-04.title: Stethoscope Sprint and Recovery
points: Confirm the funnel set's contents on arrival. If it has no flexible tubing, the build cannot happen: buy aquarium airline tubing 3/16 in (4 mm ID / 6 mm OD), about 2 ft per team.

Demo one sealed joint before kids start: insert the funnel spout into the tube end (or push the tube onto the stem) and wrap tape around the joint to make it airtight. The airtight seal is the single make-or-break factor.
Wipe the shared open tube end (earpiece) and funnel between every user; three wipe canisters are staged for the six-team cohort. Where practical, each child holds the tube end to their own ear.
Use the radial pulse at the wrist only; do not take a neck pulse. Measurement and light activity are optional, and recorder/timekeeper roles must be available.
Identify any latex-sensitive child in advance; the balloon membrane is optional and nitrile glove or plastic wrap is the non-latex substitute (nitrile gloves on hand).

Protocol: follow every health-plan or staff restriction. After optional light stepping, count wrist pulse immediately and at intervals as it trends toward the starting rate. Stop immediately and tell an adult for dizziness, chest pain, unusual trouble breathing, or feeling unwell; this is not a fitness or medical test.

PYS-05.title: Reaction Time Combine
points: Print and hand each team a cm-to-ms conversion strip (free-fall t = sqrt(2d/g)); the ruler-drop method depends on it and it is not in the deck materials list.
Stopwatches and cones in the deck list are not used by the ruler-drop method; have them on hand only if a station wants them, do not require them.
Confirm each team logs at least 10 catches and records the MEDIAN (not best single catch) for both baseline and strategy runs, so the median-to-median comparison is valid.

PYS-06.title: SONAR Slinky Showdown
points: Verify a clear floor in COE 102 and run the six teams in two waves across three measured ~3 m lanes. If tight, shorten every lane to a measured ~2 m and retain the round-trip timing method.

Mark each station with two ~5 cm tape pieces and MEASURE the actual marked length with a meterstick rather than forcing exactly 3.00 m; speed is measured distance over measured time, so any consistent marked length works.
Station card requires goggles on while the slinky is stretched (per IIHS); distribute goggles to all teams.
Use six metal slinkies if available (faster, clearer pulse, less floor friction); otherwise rotate the two waves through the available lanes. Keep at least one spare for tangles.
Stopwatch resolution is fine; the protocol is the round-trip-and-divide method, not single one-way timing.

PYS-07.title: Pinhole Precision Challenge
points: Buy one ~$6 push-pin or sewing-needle pack: on-hand sharp items (skewers, nails) are far too thick for a clean aperture. Pre-test that a pin makes a clean round hole in the foil.
Pre-cut wax/tracing paper screen squares per team (translucent through-view screen); confirm wax paper stock is on hand.
Dim COE 102 overhead lights for the viewing phase; pre-stage shared LED flashlights as bright objects, ideally with arrow/triangle/letter cut-outs taped over the lens.
Frame the precision metric to teams as 'find the BEST hole size by comparing a few,' not 'make it as small as possible' (optimal ~1/100 of aperture-to-screen distance).
Tape all box/tube seams and darken the interior near the hole to prevent light leaks that gray out contrast; keep the tube reasonably long for a larger, easier-to-judge image.
Run the pin station as a controlled, staff-supervised station; no direct-sun viewing.

PYS-08.title: Low-Ropes Force Map Relay
points: Author and print the four source-local element cards (wall-and-coin, backless-chair stand, toe-grab hop, shifted-load line walk) on on-hand 110 lb cardstock before camp; the original ropes-course cards must not be used.

Set up stations: a clear wall length, one backless chair per station, a flat taped floor line (painter/masking tape), a small reach object (coin/candy) placed about 30 to 50 cm ahead for the wall-bend, and a 200 g hooked weight for the load walk.
Spot the backless-chair stand; keep the floor clear of bags and chairs around every station.
Rotate six teams through three duplicated challenge pairs across the 80-minute block; keep each team's predict-then-test sequence intact and never turn the flat taped line into a speed race.
Score prediction accuracy and force-map quality, not speed; do not let the taped line become a race or a raised beam; do not introduce a raised 2x4 or balance board on the hard floor.

PYS-09.title: Hovercraft Hockey Hackathon
points: Confirm the COE 102 floor is smooth and hard before camp. If carpeted, run on desks/tabletops pushed together (JPL recommends a tabletop); floor-tape targets work on any hard surface.

Staff-run low-temp glue station only (no per-team guns). Use LOW-TEMP guns: high-temp warps the CD (JPL). Glue the cap's wide base flat over the CD's 15 mm center hole, then run a second bead around the whole junction and check for gaps after it cools.
Remove each cap's tamper/tear ring so the base sits flush; cover or fully seat over the CD center hole so all air is routed through the valve. A leaky seal is the #1 failure mode.
Build 1 to 2 staff demo units first so kids see a working seal and a controllable glide.
Collect ~14 to 16 recycled CDs/DVDs (6 team builds + 2 staff demos + at least 6 spares for failed joints and redesigns). DVDs work identically (same 15 mm hole).

Convert the evidence to the published rubric: glide points = round(30 x team best distance / field-best distance), capped at 30; target points = round(five-shot raw total / 6), capped at 25. If every glide distance is zero, every team gets zero glide points.
Teach the pin-hole / small-opening airflow throttle as the redesign variable: start small, open up only if it will not lift.

PYS-10.title: Spectra Sleuth Showdown
points: Bring at least one TRUE-neon plug-in night light (not an LED night light) as the line source. The kit's LED flashlights all read as a broad band, so without a neon source the matching game and sketch task (60 of 100 points) have nothing to discriminate.

Do not depend on COE 102 overhead lighting as the line source. Modern LED troffer panels give a broad band, not mercury lines. Confirm in advance whether the room still has fluorescent tubes; if so it is a free mercury-line bonus, but plan around the neon night light regardless.

Optional enrichment only: a clear-filament incandescent (prettier true rainbow) and a bare-tube spiral CFL (mercury lines) add extra cards but both need a screw socket the kit lacks. Buy an E26 cord-socket adapter only if you actually add a screw-base bulb. Skip high-voltage gas spectrum tubes entirely.
View sources from a few meters in a dimmed area for crisp lines. Use clear (not frosted) bulbs and view bare CFL spirals directly so lines are not washed out.

Enforce the existing safety rule actively: glasses are not eye protection, no flame tests, no lasers, never point at the sun. The neon night light, a 40 W clear bulb, and a CFL are all safe to view briefly through the grating.

PYS-11.title: BookBot Bin Logic Challenge
points: Use one shared tabletop judging mat plus per-team planning copies. Mark DEPOT immediately left of A1; one legal move is an orthogonal step between adjacent bins or between DEPOT and A1. Every run starts and finishes at DEPOT.
Run one team at a time on the shared judging mat. Score route cost by legal-move count before time; record missed addresses or illegal jumps as an incomplete run. Do not use full-body floor walking.
Demo one retrieval as a whole group before teams start, to surface the row/column addressing convention.

Require a written baseline route and predicted order before the timed run, then a mandatory redesign round changing exactly ONE rule (e.g. nearest-bin-first vs row-by-row sweep) so the 'defend your rule' reflection is not skipped.
Print one planning mat and order card set per team, plus one laminated shared judging mat. Clip each team's cards separately so orders and address tags do not mix.

PYS-12.title: Accessibility Ramp Rescue Lab
points: Only one set of 8 x 200 g weights exists, shared across six teams. Sequence teams through the load station one at a time while others build and run the roll check; simultaneous load testing is impossible. This is a logistics constraint, not a shortage.
Load test protocol: bridge the ramp prototype between two desks and hang/apply weight at mid-span. Start with one 200 g weight and scale up. Do NOT load weights onto the toy cart.

Roll check: hand out the pull-back cars UNWOUND (clutch disengaged, free-rolling) for the smoothness check only. Instruct kids NOT to wind the car or it self-propels and veers off the ramp. Add masking-tape side rails or a shallow foam-board channel to keep it tracking straight.

Pre-brief teams that the bare foam-board baseline is EXPECTED to sag and that the redesign (clip or glue dowels / doubled craft sticks as ribs under the deck) is the intended loop, so a sagging baseline is success-in-progress, not a fail.
Give a concrete client spec: fixed rise (e.g. 2 in) and minimum run (24 in for 1:12 slope). Post a one-line worked rise:run example on the station sign so teams can self-check.
Tiny pull-back cars are a loss/pocketing hazard (many small loose parts). Hand out a fixed count per team and collect at end; keep spares bagged.
If a heavier free-rolling cart is wanted, build a motor-free sled from craft sticks or a folded cardstock tray with a low center of mass to carry weight on a flat base. Do not load the toy car.

PYB-01.title: Pencil Pressure Safety Lab
points: Use the 8 x 200 g hooked weight set (1.6 kg) as the single load reference for every trial so baseline vs redesign are comparable.

Do NOT free-stand a sharpened pencil and balance the weight stack on it; it topples. Rest the stack on a flat-topped applicator over the target, or use a firm two-hand press to the same weight reference.
Stack 3-5 craft-foam sheets per target so the point pierces without instantly bottoming out on the cardboard backing.
Press straight down over the target only; no hands under the load. Goggles on hand. Foam only, no skin tests.

Optional only: a flattened puck of modeling clay gives a literal retained dent (one ~2 lb tub shared across six teams), but the on-hand graph-paper reframe already makes the activity run with zero purchase.
Tie the rubric to counted squares plus pierce/no-pierce rather than a qualitative dent impression.

PYB-02.title: Domino Neuron Relay
points: Hinge each tile to the ruler with a small masking-tape tab (Exploratorium method) so tiles do not slide and resets are instant when rotating teams.

Run as a backup: 28 tiles support one ~16-tile track plus rigid comparison blocks; rotate all six teams through one shared track rather than splitting the tiles. Frame the blocks as a limited transmission analogy, not literal myelin or a synapse.
Pre-cut index cards as spacers/bridges and as gap spacers so kids hit the under-tile-height spacing quickly.
Stand the Queensell game tiles rivet-side consistent on the long edge; on a taped-down flat surface the center rivet is a non-issue.
Time the baseline versus the rigid-block comparison track over the same ruler length with the owned stopwatches so the speed difference is measurable.

PYB-03.title: Pulley Rescue Relay
points: Single-kit reality: only one classroom pulley kit is owned, so PYB-03 runs as one rotating demo across six teams, not six parallel rigs. The bracket is a table-clamp (mounts to a desk edge up to ~1.25 in); no ceiling hook or ring stand is needed in COE 102.

Load: hang the 200 g hooked weights to about three-quarters of the chosen scale's max (about 350 to 400 g on the 5N scale, or 600 to 700 g on the 10N scale) to seat the rope, avoid slip, and give a clear effort drop on the 2x setup.
Scales: we own five scales (1N/5N/10N/20N/30N). Stagger the 5N and 10N across the baseline/fixed/movable steps as a rotation per TeachEngineering ('one per team if available'); no purchase needed.

Friction framing for staff: the measured 2x effort reads MORE than half the baseline (actual MA below ideal MA, roughly 5 to 15% loss per pulley). Frame this gap as efficiency/friction, not an error; use the metal low-friction pulleys for the scored measurement, not homemade spools.
If PYB-03 is deployed for six parallel teams, provide six complete rated pulley rigs; otherwise the single-kit rotating demo is the documented no-buy path.

PYB-04.title: Barcode Checksum Rescue
points: Build every 'fake' card by changing exactly ONE digit. Mod-10 catches 100% of single-digit changes, so each fake is guaranteed catchable and scoring stays fair.

If using two-digit transpositions for variety, avoid the five differ-by-5 adjacent pairs (0/5, 1/6, 2/7, 3/8, 4/9): mod-10 does NOT catch those, so the code still passes and a kid who rejects it gets wrongly marked as a false alarm.

Pin ONE format on the printed cards: 12-digit UPC-A, odd-positions-from-the-left times 3. Do NOT mix 12-digit (UPC-A) and 13-digit (EAN-13) cards in the same deck, since the multiply-by-3 row differs and yields wrong check digits.
Print a worked example on the card or board template with positions explicitly numbered/shaded so kids and the key agree on which digits are multiplied by 3.
Provide staff a pre-computed answer key listing each card's valid/invalid status to backstop scoring and arbitrate disputes.
Verify each corrupted card against the rule before printing.

For fast teams, add tiered rounds to fill the 60-min block (CS Unplugged budgets ~30 min): warm-up verify-a-valid-code, timed hunt deck, then a 'design your own fake we can still catch' round (forces single-digit changes), then explain-the-rule.

PYB-05.title: Code Break Cipher Relay
points: The whole team solves; ONE rotating runner delivers the answer, whispered or shown written, so rival teams cannot fish. A wrong answer gets 'not yet' with unlimited retries and no penalty.

Four minutes per code, ten codes. First five correct teams earn 10/8/6/4/2; any later correct answer before time earns 1; unsolved earns 0. A perfect sweep is exactly 100, so totals enter the site as a normal out-of-100 station.
Dead heat at the judge table: both teams take the higher finish slot and the next slot is skipped.
The decoder sheet is fair game the whole time; knowing which tool to grab is the skill being scored. Codes get harder round by round, and code 10 rewards a team that splits the work.
Never hand-type a ciphertext. Every slip is computed from the plaintext by the cipher functions in the print builder, so the slips and the answer key can never disagree.
Code 7 (the acrostic) counts as correct as one word or two: GOTEAMS or GO TEAMS.
Rotate the runner every code so everyone runs at least once; log the finish order as answers arrive, not after time is called.
